title: Podcast EP367: How Keysight is Accelerating RF and Microwave Design with Matthew Ozalas - Semiwiki
gist: A SemiWiki podcast with Keysight's Matthew Ozalas outlines why RF/microwave circuit design is fundamentally harder to automate than digital design — because all structures become antennas at millimeter-wave frequencies — and previews Keysight's 'Capture, Orchestrate, Accelerate' framework for applying AI to speed up the iterative RF design process.

insights.claim: At millimeter-wave frequencies and above, all circuit structures effectively become antennas, making coupling analysis and its minimization a significant engineering challenge distinct from digital circuit design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains a core technical reason RF/mmWave design (relevant to 5G/6G, radar, satellite and advanced packaging interconnects) resists the same automation approaches that have worked for digital design, implying EDA vendors need RF-specific AI tooling rather than repurposed digital-design AI.

insights.claim: RF and microwave circuit design involves an iterative, time-consuming trial-and-error engineering process that differs meaningfully from digital design workflows.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies RF design's manual, iterative nature as a specific bottleneck that AI-driven design automation tools could target for productivity gains, a potential growth vector for EDA vendors serving RF/wireless/defense markets.

insights.claim: AI can be applied to RF design to dramatically accelerate the iterative and time-consuming trial-and-error work, allowing design teams to instead focus on higher-level architectural decisions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Positions AI-assisted RF design as a productivity lever that shifts engineering time from low-level iteration to higher-value architectural work, a value proposition Keysight is using to sell AI-enabled EDA tools.

insights.claim: Keysight's proposed model for applying AI to RF design is 'Capture, Orchestrate, Accelerate,' and the company describes ongoing work and progress in this area.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A named, three-stage framework worth tracking as Keysight's competitive positioning statement in AI-driven EDA for RF design, comparable to how other EDA vendors frame their AI design-automation roadmaps.
insights.quote: The primary model Matthew proposes is “Capture, Orchestrate, Accelerate.”

insights.claim: Keysight's Matthew Ozalas has authored application notes on artificial neural network simulation models for RF power amplifiers, indicating Keysight is actively developing machine-learning-based simulation models for specific RF component classes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that Keysight's AI-for-RF push extends into published, applied research (neural network models for power amplifiers), signaling tangible R&D investment behind the marketing framework rather than a purely conceptual pitch.
